text:
Aisha: Picking up from the alloc-hints threads 1 1 — proposal: collapse lifetime+avoid_compaction into a small ResidencyPolicy enum + a numeric CompactPriority (0-100) so the allocator has a single decision vector. Example: ResidencyPolicy::HotSticky, HotAdvisory, ColdArchive. CompactPriority defaults: HotSticky=80, HotAdvisory=40, ColdArchive=5.

Tom: Can you show the proposed API surface?

Aisha: ```cpp
// simple C ABI for alloc2 compatibility
enum ResidencyPolicy { HotSticky, HotAdvisory, ColdArchive };
struct AllocAttrs {
  ResidencyPolicy residency;
  uint8_t compact_priority; // 0..100
  uint16_t expected_access_rate_per_min; // best-effort
  uint8_t hint_version; // rolling forward flags
};
// alloc2(owner_id, size, &AllocAttrs) -> handle
```

Ravi: Numeric compact_priority is nice for gradualism. But exposing 0-100 per alloc risks being misused by users. I think we should expose only presets in public SDKs and keep numeric for internal/ops.

Nora: Agreed. Public SDKs should only accept presets; internal binary can map presets -> compact_priority. Also add a server-side override table per-tenant.

Ben: Two operational concerns: 1) fragmentation budget when many HotSticky allocations accumulate, and 2) interaction with live compaction. Suggest we add a demotion-grace-period and a compaction-throttle token-bucket tied to throughput SLO.

Aisha: Good call. Proposed runtime rules: 1) HotSticky: try to keep >90% resident but allow demote after demotion-grace-period (default 48h idle) if fragmentation pressure high. 2) HotAdvisory: prefer GPU while lightly evictable. 3) ColdArchive: prefer host-compress/remote NUMA. Compaction-throttle: token-bucket refilled by tokens proportional to spare capacity; max tokens per second bounded by p99 tail budget.

Tom: Need telemetry first: alloc_policy_decision{preset, tenant, outcome=kept|demoted|evicted}, fragmentation_index{tenant, window}, compaction_throttle_utilization. Also add tracepoints for compaction start/stop and demote actions.

Ravi: How does KV-cache interact? If an alloc is pinned but holds KV entries, demotion could invalidate cache semantics. We must surface an attach flag: kv_affinity=true which bumps compact_priority automatically.

Nora: Also check Private deployment defaults: companies with strict latency SLAs probably want HotSticky by default for model-serving routes; but we need an admin opt-out. Document in deployment guide.

Ben: Backward compatibility: implement alloc2 as wrapper that reads hint_version; if hint_version missing, map to HotAdvisory. SDK migration plan: v1 clients remain HotAdvisory.

Aisha: Rollout plan: 0) telemetry-only (SDK sends hints but runtime ignores), 1) soft-apply (runtime uses hints but demote allowed under pressure), 2) tenant-level enforcement via config, 3) promote numeric controls for ops only. Each stage 2-4 weeks with Canary jobs.

Tom: Experiments matrix: microbench workloads (chat_long, embedding_bulk, realtime_tiny) run 1h each with: baseline, soft-apply, enforce-tenant. Measure: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, fragmentation_index, demote_rate, eviction_rate.

Ravi: I'll sketch a demote-worker prototype that: scans sticky candidates, computes fragmentation delta if kept vs demoted, then applies demote if delta reduces fragmentation beyond threshold. It will call host-compress flow instead of full spill when possible.

Nora: One more: compaction race hazard. We should gate compaction to only run on nodes with low active inference load; coordinator must query load signals. Add compaction-safe-window and compaction-shrink-threshold.

Aisha: Will add to RFC: API shape, presets, telemetry schema, compaction-throttle algorithm (token-bucket pseudo), demote-worker heuristics, KV-affinity flag, rollout plan, and SDK compatibility notes. Posting PR after I wire telemetry.

infra-bot: deploy/alloc2-telemetry canary succeeded 2026-03-21T11:02:03Z :white_check_mark:

Tom: Thanks, also add regression alert: if p99 latency increases >10% or fragmentation_index increases >15% during soft-apply, rollback auto.

Ravi: I'll add unit tests for mapping preset -> compact_priority and an integration test that simulates many HotSticky allocs under limited GPU.

Ben: Let's also include an ops playbook: how to force-demote a tenant, how to run online compaction safely, and emergency steps when fragmentation causes OOMs.

Aisha: Perfect. I'll update RFC and add a short FAQ about "why numeric priority exists but is hidden". PR ETA: Tue. Cheers :rocket:
